I used to think a debate was something you could win.

In tenth grade I argued, for six rounds in a row, that cities should ban cars from their centers. I won five of them. Then in the sixth round a girl from another school asked me a question I couldn't answer: "Who cleans your downtown at 3 a.m., and how do they get there?"

I didn't know. I'd read 14 articles and none of them mentioned her.

So I went and looked. It turned out that in my own city the night-shift cleaning crews mostly drive in from two counties away, because the last bus leaves at 11:40. My plan would have made their commute impossible, and I'd never noticed they existed.

I still think the plan is mostly right. But "mostly" is doing more work in that sentence than it used to, and I've stopped trusting any argument of mine that nobody has tried hard to break.
